title: Shard-conservative fanout throttler and hybrid stitcher for oversized cohort queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Large cohort queries in the Console analytics path are causing high read amplification and extreme tail latency when a single query fanouts across many shard workers. This ticket implements an admission-control style fanout throttler plus a hybrid stitching approach that reduces redundant work, enables progressive result delivery, and leverages compacted micro-aggregation at shard proxies to lower IOPS and network churn.
problem_statement: Observed symptoms: (1) cohort queries that touch >500 shards spike 95th and 99th percentiles for query latency and increase cluster CPU/IO contention; (2) repeated overlapping subqueries across tenants produce duplicate reads for the same time windows; (3) current hedging/prefetch heuristics either over-hedge or under-protect, leading to wasted resources or missed SLOs. Need a solution that reduces tail latency and read amplification while preserving accuracy and progressive UX for Console users.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Shard-Conservative Fanout Throttler in the query planner that uses lightweight cardinality estimates and heat-index hints to admit shards in prioritized waves. Complement this with a Hybrid Stitcher: small partial results are returned early from high-priority shards while lower-priority shard results get compacted into micro-aggregates and stitched server-side to form the final response. Add an optional sampled-mode fallback (percentile-based sampling) for very large cohorts to provide immediate approximate insights with a full result delivered asynchronously.
implementation_plan: Add fanout admission module to query planner: cardinality estimator + per-tenant rate budget
Create shard prioritization function using recent query heat maps and time-window density
Implement hybrid stitcher in aggregator service to accept partials and compact lower-priority shard payloads
Introduce shard-proxy micro-aggregation endpoint to produce bucketed summaries for low-priority shards
Add progressive-response protocol (streaming chunked partial + final stitched) to dashboard API
Instrument new metrics and dashboards: fanout_count, admitted_shards, stitch_latency, aggregate_compression_ratio
Ship safety toggle behind feature flag and run canary on 10% of Console traffic, then ramp with smoke tests
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for cohort queries (>500 shards) reduced by at least 30% in canary region
Average read amplification (shard reads per logical result) reduced by >= 25% for targeted cohort workloads
No customer-facing errors or data inconsistency incidents during 72-hour canary
Progressive response shown in Console: partial results appear within SLA for 90% of large-cohort queries
Feature flag allows immediate rollback with <5 minutes of degraded traffic routing
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and prioritization heuristics
Integration tests for hybrid stitcher correctness under partial delivery and out-of-order shard returns
Load tests that simulate heavy cohort queries with realistic shard cardinalities to validate reduction in IOPS and tail latency
Canary run on non-critical workspace running A/B with control group and real usage patterns
Chaos tests toggling delayed shard proxies to validate progressive assembly and timeouts
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag off to stop admission control and stitching; fall back to current hedging/prefetch path. Monitor for restoration of baseline metrics and abort ramp if error rate exceeds 0.5% or if latency regressions >10% persist after rollback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect cardinality estimates cause biased prioritization -> Mitigation: conservative default to avoid dropping hot shards and safety throttle to admit at least X% of shards

Risk: stitching introduces consistency anomalies when shard partials overlap -> Mitigation: enforce deterministic merge ordering and idempotent shard payloads, include vector clock for window coverage
Risk: increased CPU on aggregator from compacting micro-aggregates -> Mitigation: move heavy compaction to shard proxies and cap aggregator parallelism with circuit breaker
Risk: UX confusion from progressive results showing transient values -> Mitigation: add explicit Console indicator that final result is pending and surface sampling/exact mode labels
